name: PD 760 was established by Ordinance No. 26860, passed by the Dallas City Council on June 27,
source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 760 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-760.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 760 was established by Ordinance No. 26860, passed by the Dallas City Council on June 27, 2007. (Ord. 26860)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-760.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 760 is established on property located south of Walton Walker Boulevard, fronting approximately 1007.11 feet on the west line of Ledbetter Drive. The size of PD 760 is approximately 43.4937 acres. (Ord. 26860)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-760.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 26860)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-760.104. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 760A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 26860)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-760.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

A development plan must be approved by the city plan commission as required by Section 51A- 4.702, and must be reviewed by the escarpment committee and the director under the review process for an escarpment permit as set forth in Section 51A-5.204, before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this district. (Ord. 26860)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-760.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted in this district are those main uses permitted in the various districts shown on the conceptual plan, subject to the same conditions applicable in the respective district, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the R- 10(A) Single Family District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in the areas in this district designated on the conceptual plan as R-10(A) only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review
(DIR) in the R-10(A) Single Family District is subject to DIR in the areas in this district designated on the conceptual plan as R-10(A); etc.

(b) A private recreation center, club or area is permitted by right.

(c) Private streets or alleys are permitted by right. (Ord. 26860)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-760.107. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A- 4.217.

(b) The following accessory uses are not permitted:

-- Accessory helistop. -- Accessory medical/infectious waste incinerator. -- Accessory outside display of merchandise. -- Accessory outside sales. -- Accessory pathological waste incinerator. (Ord. 26860)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-760.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A- 4.400, this section controls.)

(a) Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the various districts in Chapter 51A apply in the various districts shown on the conceptual plan. For example, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the R-10(A) Single Family District apply in the areas shown on the conceptual plan as R-10(A); etc.

(b) Maximum number of dwelling units in areas designated as CH and TH-3(A) on the conceptual plan are as shown on the conceptual plan.

(c) No construction is permitted in the area shown as open space on the conceptual plan. (Ord. 26860)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-760.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

Consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use. (Ord. 26860)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-760.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 26860)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-760.111. LANDSCAPING.

(a) For nonresidential uses, a landscape plan must be submitted with the development plan and approved by the city plan commission before issuance of a building permit to authorize work in this district.

(b) For residential uses, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(c) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 26860)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-760.112. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 26860)

sections.title: Street Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-760.113. STREET STANDARDS.

(a) For private streets in the TH-3(A) and CH areas shown on the conceptual plan, the following street standards apply:

(1) Minimum pavement width is 33 feet, measured from face-of-curb to face-of- curb.

(2) Minimum right-of-way width is 53 feet.

(b) For private streets in the R-7.5(A), R-10(A), and R-1/2 ac(A) areas shown on the conceptual plan, the following street standards apply:

(1) Minimum pavement width is 26 feet, measured from face-of-curb to face-of- curb.

(2) Minimum right-of-way width is 50 feet.

(c) Access to the Property is permitted from Ledbetter Drive only.

(d) Access easements are permitted in the areas shown on the conceptual plan, subject to approval of the design by the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. 26860)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-760.114. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 26860)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-760.115. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this district until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 26860)

sections.title: Zoning Map
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-760.116. ZONING MAP.

PD 760 is located on Zoning Map No. M-4. (Ord. 26860)
